creative_intent: Generate a precision product photograph of a front-facing, engineered, matte white boron-carbide ceramic industrial component, focusing on its exact symmetrical hard-surface geometry, clean beveled edges, and visible mounting holes, while maintaining a clear industrial object silhouette in a premium studio isolation setting with controlled shadows and minimal environment. The primary focus is on achieving a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, emphasizing dry, dense, and tactile ceramic properties with subtle mineral surface variation, strictly avoiding any decorative, organic, consumer gadget, or fashion styling.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

material.finish: precision-manufactured, dry, dense, tactile ceramic density, subtle mineral surface variation

constraints: color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Abstract composition issues leading to subject loss
Loss of clear manufactured object readability
Material drift towards forbidden reads (e.g., plaster, glossy plastic)
Failure to maintain material-only scope while preserving object identity
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Preserve manufactured object readability at all costs
Ensure material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read
Suppress any decorative, organic, consumer gadget, or fashion styling
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
success_criteria: Clean matte B4C technical ceramic read is achieved
Dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability is evident
Material-only scope is preserved without losing the manufactured object read
The object's identity as a boron-carbide ceramic housing is unmistakable
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
direction_summary: Focus on a front-facing, matte boron-carbide ceramic industrial component in a studio setting. Prioritize a clean, dry, dense technical ceramic material read, ensuring the manufactured object's precise geometry and silhouette are clearly visible. Strictly avoid abstract compositions, material drift, and any non-industrial styling.
